The test image shows a cut tomato stem placed in a glass beaker of water, with white milky/slimy bacterial ooze streaming down from the cut end into the water. The stem cross-section shows internal brown vascular discoloration. This is the classic "ooze test" diagnostic for bacterial wilt. Primary candidate: **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**.

Let me view reference images across 8 classes.
Southern_Bacterial_Wilt stem reference shows brown/tan internal vascular discoloration matching the test image stem. Let me check Bacterial_Wilt next.
Bacterial_Wilt Bugwood_11 shows a similar beaker setup but NO streaming ooze (negative test). The test image has distinct white streaming ooze. Let me check Bacterial_Wilt Bugwood_3.

**Bacterial_Wilt Bugwood_3** is nearly identical to the test image - same beaker ooze test, white streaming bacterial ooze, brown vascular discoloration, similar image numbering (5606063 vs test's 5606065). Very strong match. Let me check one more Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference.
Southern_Bacterial_Wilt whole_plant shows wilting - not the ooze test setup. I need 4 more class views. Let me continue.

Early_Blight, Late_Blight, and Verticillium_Wilt all show leaf lesions - completely different from the beaker ooze test setup.

**Summary of analysis:**

- Test image (ID: 5606065): Cut stem in a 500ml beaker, white milky bacterial ooze streaming downward into clear water, brown vascular discoloration in stem cross-section — classic positive bacterial ooze test
- **Bacterial_Wilt/Bugwood_3 (ID: 5606063)**: Nearly identical — same beaker, same bacterial streaming pattern, same brown stem discoloration, sequential image IDs from same source
- Bacterial_Wilt/Bugwood_11: Same beaker setup but NO streaming (different result, possibly negative control)
- Southern_Bacterial_Wilt references show split stem or whole plant wilting — not the ooze test
- All other classes (canker, leaf blights, wilts) show completely different visual presentations

The test image is visually identical to the Bacterial_Wilt reference (Bugwood_3), with sequential image IDs indicating same source/photographer demonstrating the same diagnostic procedure.
